title: Tapered Fibre Fabry-Pérot Cavities for the Generation of Near-Visible, Phase-locked, and Broadband Kerr Frequency Combs
authors: Matthew Macnaughtan, Yiqing Xu, Miro Erkintalo, Stéphane Coen, Stuart G. Murdoch
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of near-visible, broadband Kerr frequency combs using a tapered fibre Fabry-Pérot resonator. By incorporating micron-diameter tapered silica fibre into a pulsed-driven Fabry-Pérot configuration, we exploit geometric dispersion engineering to overcome the strong normal dispersion intrinsic to silica (and nearly all materials) at short wavelengths, achieving net anomalous dispersion in the near-visible regime. The strong mode confinement of the tapered fibre simultaneously enhances the Kerr nonlinearity by over an order of magnitude relative to standard fibre, substantially reducing the threshold drive power for nonlinear structure formation. Through precise control of the cavity fabrication, we experimentally demonstrate and numerically confirm a rich suite of coherent, phase-locked nonlinear structures, including conventional anomalous dispersion cavity solitons, zero dispersion solitons with spectral bandwidths exceeding 16 THz between 750 nm and 800 nm, as well as switching wave combs and broadband Raman solitons, the latter also reported here for the first time in the near-visible regime. Our results establish the tapered fibre Fabry-Pérot resonator as a versatile platform for near-visible and potentially visible coherent frequency comb generation.
summary: This paper reports on using a Tapered Fibre Fabry-Pérot resonator to generate broadband, phase-locked Kerr frequency combs in the near-visible spectrum. By engineering the fibre's dispersion and leveraging enhanced nonlinearity, the authors successfully demonstrated multiple nonlinear states, including zero-dispersion and Raman solitons. This establishes the TFFP resonator as a versatile platform for advanced coherent light source development.
main_problem: The primary goal is the generation of near-visible, phase-locked, and broadband Kerr frequency combs.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the generation of a full suite of coherent nonlinear structures, including zero-dispersion solitons and Raman solitons, in the near-visible regime using a tapered fibre Fabry-Pérot resonator.
method: The technique involves engineering the dispersion profile of a Fabry-Pérot cavity by incorporating a tapered silica fibre, which enhances nonlinearity and controls the dispersion regime.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Tapered Fibre Fabry-Pérot (TFFP) resonator. The key mechanism relies on geometric dispersion engineering to achieve net anomalous or near-zero dispersion in the near-visible regime, while the tapered geometry enhances the Kerr nonlinearity significantly.
key_observables: Broadband spectral profiles, cavity solitons (CSs), zero-dispersion solitons (ZDSs), switching wave combs, and Raman solitons.
important_parameters: Near-visible wavelength (e.g., 770.5 nm), high Kerr nonlinearity enhancement ($>10	imes$), and the ability to tune the dispersion ($ eta_2$) across anomalous, zero, and normal regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the fundamental mode is exclusively used, which helps maintain spectral cleanliness by preventing avoided-mode crossings.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, the engineered dispersion ($ ar{ eta}_2$ vs. $\lambda$), and pseudo-colour spectral maps and profiles confirming the existence of different soliton types (CS, ZDS, SW, RS) across varying cavity detunings.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the TFFP platform as a versatile tool, demonstrating the generation of various nonlinear structures (CSs, ZDSs, SW combs, RSs) by actively controlling the cavity dispersion regime through fibre tapering and detuning scans.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it demonstrates precise control over nonlinear wave dynamics (solitons and combs) in a highly tunable, low-loss optical cavity platform, which is crucial for quantum light sources.
